introduction: "There is none other God but Him" is the sentence these passages turn over. They say that God is one, not as the first of a series of numbers, with no partner, likeness, equal or opposite; that his own testimony to his oneness is the only adequate one; that every created thing bears witness to it; and that to acknowledge it is the gift for which a believer gives thanks. Most of the readings are prayers and affirmations, many of them by the Báb. Beside them stand a hundred voices: the Shema, the prophets and the Psalms, the Qur’an's chapter of Unity and Throne Verse, Paul and John, an Upanishad, the Tao Te Ching, Xenophanes, Aristotle, Plotinus and Maimonides, with Hume and Gibbon on what monotheism has cost and the Nicene Creed for another way of confessing one God.
questions: "Thou art the One, not in the numerical sense." Maimonides says something close. What is being denied when God is said not to be one as a number is one?
Many passages say that only God's own testimony to his unity is adequate, and that all things nevertheless testify to it. How can both be so?
The Báb's prayers insist on no consort, no son, no partner; the Nicene Creed was written to defend the unity of God. Where exactly do the two confessions differ?
Hume thought belief in one God tends to intolerance, and Gibbon admired Rome's easy plurality. What in these readings would resist turning oneness into exclusion?
One passage prescribes saying "There is no God but God" nineteen times a night. Jesus warned against vain repetitions and Tagore against the telling of beads. What makes repetition a remembrance?
James says the devils also believe that God is one. What follows in a life from really holding it?

outside.why: The Tao Te Ching says that the Tao produced One, One produced Two, Two produced Three, and Three produced all things.
Plotinus describes the One as perfect and lacking nothing, and all that is as its overflowing.
An Upanishad says that in the beginning there was only that which is, one only, without a second.
Maimonides makes the same distinction: God is one, but not as one of a kind or as a body is one, and with a unity found nowhere in the world.
Isaiah uses the potter and the clay to mark the distance between maker and thing made.
The letter to the Hebrews speaks of one who is the brightness of God's glory and the express image of his person.
Zophar asks Job whether anyone can find out the Almighty to perfection.
Solomon, dedicating the temple, confesses that the heaven of heavens cannot contain God.
The Qur’an tells how Abraham looked at a star and said, "This is my Lord," and when it set said, "I love not things that set."
Xenophanes, a century before Socrates, spoke of one god, greatest among gods and men, unlike mortals in form or thought.
John's Gospel says that the Word was with God and was God. How does this passage's account of meanings that are one with the Truth compare with that verse?
The Qur’an names God the First and the Last, the Outward and the Inward.
At the burning bush the name given to Moses is: I AM THAT I AM.
The Tao Te Ching begins by saying that the name that can be named is not the enduring name.
The Qur’an says that by whatever name God is called, his are the most beautiful names.
Deuteronomy says that the Lord is God, and there is none else beside him.
A psalm says that the Lord is great and greatly to be praised, and that his greatness is unsearchable.
In the Qur’an the voice at the bush says: I am God; there is no god save me.
Isaiah hears: I am the first, and I am the last; and beside me there is no God.
A psalm says that heaven and earth shall be changed like a garment, but thou art the same.
Isaiah has God ask: to whom then will ye liken me, or shall I be equal?
The Qur’an says that nothing is like him, and that he is the Hearer and the Seer.
The first of the commandments is: thou shalt have no other gods before me.
Hume observed that religions which maintain the unity of God have been intolerant, and polytheists the reverse. What in these passages on oneness would encourage that, and what would forbid it?

Gibbon wrote that in Rome all modes of worship were equally true to the people, equally false to the philosopher and equally useful to the magistrate. What is lost in that easy peace, and what was kept by it?
Isaiah hears: I am God, and there is none else; I am God, and there is none like me.
A psalm says: among the gods there is none like thee; thou art God alone.
A psalm has God say of himself: be still, and know that I am God.
The Qur’an says that everything will perish save his countenance, and that to him all are returned.
Jesus says: I and my Father are one. Christians and Muslims have read that sentence very differently. How does this passage speak of oneness known through the Manifestation?
The Rig Veda says that the sages call by many names what is one.
Symmachus pleaded with a Christian emperor that so great a mystery cannot be reached by one road only. How does "grace hath encompassed all religions" answer his plea?
Pope addresses the Father of all, adored in every age and clime by saint, savage and sage.
This is the verse of the Qur’an that the passage echoes: if there were gods beside God, heaven and earth would be in disorder.
Aristotle ends his account of the first principle with a line of Homer: the rule of many is not good; one ruler let there be.
A psalm says that the heavens declare the glory of God and the sky shows his handiwork.
Job says: ask the beasts and the birds and the earth, and they will tell whose hand has made this.
The Qur’an says that there is not a thing that does not hymn his praise.
Paul says that the invisible things of God are seen through the things that are made.
Augustine asked earth, sea and sky, and each answered that it was not God but had been made by him.
Jesus says that if his disciples were silent, the stones would cry out.
Proverbs calls the spirit of man the candle of the Lord, which searches the inward parts.
The confession of Israel is one sentence: hear, O Israel, the Lord our God is one Lord.
Deuteronomy asks that these words be spoken when sitting at home and walking, lying down and rising up.
The Qur’an tells believers to remember God with much remembrance, and to glorify him morning and evening.
Paul asks the Thessalonians to rejoice always, to pray without ceasing and to give thanks in everything.
The Qur’an says that in the remembrance of God hearts find rest.
Jesus warns against vain repetitions, as though one were heard for much speaking. What makes a repeated phrase more than that?
Tagore tells the worshipper to leave his chanting and telling of beads and find God where the tiller tills the ground. What can repetition do, and what can it replace?
The letter of James remarks that the devils also believe that God is one, and tremble. What is the difference between saying the sentence and being changed by it?
The Qur’an tells Christians: say not "Three"; God is only one God, far removed from having a son.

The Nicene Creed confesses the Son as God of God, Light of Light, of one substance with the Father. Those who framed it believed they were defending the unity of God. Where exactly do they and this prayer part?
Paul says that though many are called gods, to us there is but one God, of whom are all things.
The first letter to Timothy says: one God, and one mediator between God and men. How do these readings speak of a mediator without a partner?
The Qur’an says: your God is one God; there is no god save him.
The Qur’an says that his are the most beautiful names, and that all in heaven and earth glorify him.
David prays: thine, O Lord, is the greatness and the power and the glory; all that is in heaven and earth is thine.
The Qur’an says that vision does not comprehend him, but he comprehends all vision.
The Throne Verse of the Qur’an praises God as the Living, the Eternal, whom neither slumber nor sleep overtakes.
This is the chapter of the Qur’an that the prayer echoes: he begets not, nor was begotten, and there is none comparable to him.
Spinoza also held that there is one self-subsisting being and nothing beside it, and concluded that all things are in God. How does the oneness confessed here differ from his?
Isaiah says that God's ways are as far above ours as the heavens above the earth.
Paul speaks of one who is the image of the invisible God.
Jesus tells a Samaritan woman that God is to be worshipped neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem, but in spirit and in truth.
A psalm says: I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help.
The Revelation of John has God say: I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending.
This is the verse quoted: God bears witness that there is no god but him, and so do the angels and those who have knowledge.
A psalm says: whom have I in heaven but thee? and there is none on earth that I desire beside thee.
The Qur’an says that wherever you turn, there is the face of God.
Paul exclaims at the depth of the wisdom of God, whose ways are past finding out.
The opening chapter of the Qur’an is such a praise, and asks to be shown the straight path.
Proverbs says that the one who acknowledges God in all his ways will have his paths made straight.
When Peter made his confession Jesus told him that flesh and blood had not revealed it to him.
Isaiah says that the people who walked in darkness have seen a great light.
The Qur’an tells of a testimony given before time: am I not your Lord? They said: yes, we testify.
Jesus says that not everyone who says "Lord, Lord" will enter the kingdom, but the one who does the Father's will. What does a confession of oneness commit a person to?
Jesus says to Philip that whoever has seen him has seen the Father.
Paul thanks God at every remembrance of those to whom he writes.
The elder of John's letters has no greater joy than to hear that his children walk in truth.
Milton's Abdiel is praised for being faithful alone among the faithless, when every other turned away.
Paul speaks of one God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in all.
Isaiah heard the seraphim cry: holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts.
Zechariah foretells a day when the Lord shall be king over all the earth, one Lord, and his name one.
Tennyson ends his elegy with one God, one law, one element, and one far-off divine event.
Kabir sings that God first created the light, and from the one light the whole universe came.
The Tao Te Ching says that the one who knows does not speak.
The Qur’an says: truth has come and falsehood has vanished away, for falsehood is bound to vanish.
A psalm says that the secret of the Lord is with those who fear him.
Paul says that now we see through a glass darkly, and then face to face.
Jesus says that the pure in heart are blessed, for they shall see God.
The priestly blessing asks that the Lord make his face shine upon his people.
Moses saw a bush that burned with fire and was not consumed.
Jesus says that he came to cast fire on the earth, and longs for it to be kindled.
Three young men refused to bow to a golden image, whatever the king might do.
Elijah, alone against the prophets of Baal, asked the people how long they would waver between two opinions.
A psalm prays that the beauty of the Lord be upon us, and that he establish the work of our hands.
Malachi asks: have we not all one father? has not one God created us? why do we deal treacherously with one another?
Jesus prays that all who believe may be one, as he and the Father are one.
The Song of Songs says that the winter is past and the flowers appear on the earth.
Daniel foretells a kingdom set up by the God of heaven that shall stand for ever.

isaiah-to-whom-will-ye-liken-me.text: To whom then will ye liken me, or shall I be equal? saith the Holy One. Lift up your eyes on high, and behold who hath created these things, that bringeth out their host by number: he calleth them all by names by the greatness of his might, for that he is strong in power; not one faileth

isaiah-none-like-me.text: Remember the former things of old: for I am God, and there is none else; I am God, and there is none like me

corinthians-but-one-god.text: As concerning therefore the eating of those things that are offered in sacrifice unto idols, we know that an idol is nothing in the world, and that there is none other God but one. For though there be that are called gods, whether in heaven or in earth, (as there be gods many, and lords many,) But to us there is but one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and we in him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, by whom are all things, and we by him

isaiah-clay-and-the-potter.text: Woe unto him that striveth with his Maker! Let the potsherd strive with the potsherds of the earth. Shall the clay say to him that fashioneth it, What makest thou? or thy work, He hath no hands

thessalonians-pray-without-ceasing.text: Rejoice evermore. Pray without ceasing. In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you

zechariah-one-lord-and-his-name-one.text: And the Lord shall be king over all the earth: in that day shall there be one Lord, and his name one

malachi-have-we-not-all-one-father.text: Have we not all one father? hath not one God created us? why do we deal treacherously every man against his brother, by profaning the covenant of our fathers

john-that-they-all-may-be-one.text: That they all may be one; as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee, that they also may be one in us: that the world may believe that thou hast sent me

john-i-and-my-father-are-one.text: I and my Father are one

deuteronomy-none-else-beside-him.text: Unto thee it was shewed, that thou mightest know that the Lord he is God; there is none else beside him

psalm-thou-art-god-alone.text: Among the gods there is none like unto thee, O Lord; neither are there any works like unto thy works. All nations whom thou hast made shall come and worship before thee, O Lord; and shall glorify thy name. For thou art great, and doest wondrous things: thou art God alone

quran-gods-beside-allah-disordered.text: If there were therein gods beside Allah, then verily both (the heavens and the earth) had been disordered. Glorified be Allah, the Lord of the Throne, from all that they ascribe (unto Him).

quran-your-god-is-one-god.text: Your Allah is One Allah; there is no Allah save Him, the Beneficent, the Merciful.

quran-remember-with-much-remembrance.text: O ye who believe! Remember Allah with much remembrance.

quran-i-love-not-things-that-set.text: When the night grew dark upon him he beheld a star. He said: This is my Lord. But when it set, he said: I love not things that set.

aristotle-one-ruler-let-there-be.text: The rule of many is not good; one ruler let there be
aristotle-one-ruler-let-there-be.author: Aristotle

chandogya-one-only-without-a-second.text: only that which is, was in the beginning, one only, without a second

maimonides-not-two-or-more-but-one.text: This God is one. He is not two or more, but one, unified in a manner which [surpasses] any unity that is found in the world; i.e., He is not one in the manner of a general category which includes many individual entities, nor one in the way that the body is divided into different portions and dimensions
maimonides-not-two-or-more-but-one.author: Moses Maimonides
maimonides-not-two-or-more-but-one.work: Mishneh Torah, Foundations of the Torah

hume-intolerance-of-unity.text: The intolerance of almost all religions, which have maintained the unity of god, is as remarkable as the contrary principle in polytheists
hume-intolerance-of-unity.author: David Hume
